# knittogether

knittogether lets you write a report with colleagues who work in Word or
PowerPoint, while you keep the numbers, charts and tables in R. They
keep writing in Office. You keep your analysis reproducible. Nobody
copies and pastes.

## Why

Most reports need two kinds of work: someone who knows the subject
writes the words, and someone else produces the analysis. A lot of time
goes on the hand-over. Charts get pasted into Word and reformatted,
slide breaks get fixed, citations get redone. Then the data changes, or
someone rewrites a paragraph, and it all starts again.

With knittogether, the writer types a placeholder such as
`placeholder_plot` where a chart should go. You convert the Word file to
Markdown, fill each placeholder from R, and render the result with
Quarto to Word, PowerPoint, HTML or PDF. The writer can keep editing in
Word, and you can bring their changes back in without losing the R
output. Text, images, tables, citations, footnotes and slide breaks all
survive the trip.

## Installation

``` r

# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("wyuill/knittogether")
```

Reading PowerPoint files needs Pandoc 3.8.3 or later. Recent versions of
RStudio, Positron and Quarto include one, and knittogether will find it.
For citations you also need [Zotero](https://www.zotero.org/download)
with the [Better BibTeX](https://retorque.re/zotero-better-bibtex/)
add-on.
[`vignette("citations")`](https://wyuill.github.io/knittogether/articles/citations.md)
explains how to set this up.

## How it works

``` mermaid
flowchart LR
  A["Writer adds placeholders<br/>in the Word draft"] --> B["Coder: convert, clean,<br/>replace_placeholders()"]
  B --> C["Writer edits the draft<br/>in Word, around the R output"]
  C --> D["Coder: convert, clean with<br/>clear_draft, replace again"]
  D --> C
  D --> E["Final render with<br/>draft_mode = FALSE"]
```

1.  The writer types placeholders into the Word draft wherever R output
    should go.
2.  You convert the draft to Markdown, tidy it up and fill in the
    placeholders.
3.  The writer edits the draft in Word, writing around your output.
4.  You bring their edits back in and refresh the R output. Steps 3 and
    4 repeat as often as you need.
5.  When the words are final, you render the finished report.

Either of you can start. You can also begin from a Quarto document and
send it to Word for the first round of writing.

## Example

Say the writer’s draft contains `placeholder_total` and
`placeholder_plot`:

``` r

library(knittogether)

convert_markdown("draft.docx", markdown_file = "draft.md")
clean_markdown("draft.md", placeholder_prefix = "placeholder_")

total <- define_content(
  placeholder_id = "total",
  output_mode = "inline",
  content = { nrow(mtcars) }
)
plot <- define_content(
  placeholder_id = "plot",
  output_mode = "chunk",
  content = { plot(mtcars$wt, mtcars$mpg) },
  chunk_options = list(echo = FALSE)
)

replace_placeholders(
  "draft.md",
  placeholder_prefix = "placeholder_",
  code_content = placeholder_map(specs = list(total, plot))
)
```

`draft.md` now has inline R code where `placeholder_total` was and an R
chunk where `placeholder_plot` was. Include it in a Quarto document and
render it to any format.

[`vignette("knittogether")`](https://wyuill.github.io/knittogether/articles/knittogether.md)
goes through this step by step, including how to bring the writer’s
edits back in.

## Getting help

Every function has a help page, for example
[`?clean_markdown`](https://wyuill.github.io/knittogether/reference/clean_markdown.md).
If something doesn’t work, [open an
issue](https://github.com/LBCamden/knittogether/issues) or [get in
touch](https://jsna.camden.gov.uk/about/#get-in-touch).

# Package index

## Workflow

Bring a Word or PowerPoint file into Markdown, fill its placeholders and
tidy it for Quarto.

- [`convert_markdown()`](https://wyuill.github.io/knittogether/reference/convert_markdown.md)
  : Convert a Word or PowerPoint file to Markdown
- [`clean_markdown()`](https://wyuill.github.io/knittogether/reference/clean_markdown.md)
  : Tidy converted Markdown for Quarto
- [`replace_placeholders()`](https://wyuill.github.io/knittogether/reference/replace_placeholders.md)
  : Fill placeholders with R content
- [`run_workflow()`](https://wyuill.github.io/knittogether/reference/run_workflow.md)
  : Convert, clean and fill a document in one call

## Defining content

Say what goes in each placeholder.

- [`define_content()`](https://wyuill.github.io/knittogether/reference/define_content.md)
  : Describe the content for one placeholder
- [`placeholder_map()`](https://wyuill.github.io/knittogether/reference/placeholder_map.md)
  : Collect the content for every placeholder

## Versions

Pick up the latest draft and keep earlier ones.

- [`latest_word_file()`](https://wyuill.github.io/knittogether/reference/latest_word_file.md)
  : Find the newest Word or PowerPoint file in a folder
- [`timestamped_path()`](https://wyuill.github.io/knittogether/reference/timestamped_path.md)
  : Add the date and time to a file name

## PowerPoint

Slide breaks, columns and backgrounds for slides.

- [`slide_break()`](https://wyuill.github.io/knittogether/reference/slide_break.md)
  : Start a new slide
- [`insert_slide_break()`](https://wyuill.github.io/knittogether/reference/insert_slide_break.md)
  : Break text into a new slide once, before a character limit
- [`auto_slide_break()`](https://wyuill.github.io/knittogether/reference/auto_slide_break.md)
  : Break text into slides that fit
- [`pptx_col_start()`](https://wyuill.github.io/knittogether/reference/pptx_col_start.md)
  [`pptx_col_break()`](https://wyuill.github.io/knittogether/reference/pptx_col_start.md)
  [`pptx_col_end()`](https://wyuill.github.io/knittogether/reference/pptx_col_start.md)
  : Split a slide into two columns
- [`pptx_section_slide()`](https://wyuill.github.io/knittogether/reference/pptx_section_slide.md)
  : Write a heading with a background image
- [`add_pptx_backgrounds_to_headers()`](https://wyuill.github.io/knittogether/reference/add_pptx_backgrounds_to_headers.md)
  : Add a background image to headings in Markdown

## Output format

Do something only for one output format, or hide markers in HTML.

- [`is_pptx()`](https://wyuill.github.io/knittogether/reference/is_html.md)
  [`is_docx()`](https://wyuill.github.io/knittogether/reference/is_html.md)
  [`is_pdf()`](https://wyuill.github.io/knittogether/reference/is_html.md)
  [`is_html()`](https://wyuill.github.io/knittogether/reference/is_html.md)
  : Check the format being rendered
- [`output_type()`](https://wyuill.github.io/knittogether/reference/output_type.md)
  : Name the format being rendered
- [`hide_markers_css()`](https://wyuill.github.io/knittogether/reference/hide_markers_css.md)
  : CSS that hides placeholder markers in HTML

## Checking and long documents

- [`accessibility_scan()`](https://wyuill.github.io/knittogether/reference/accessibility_scan.md)
  : Check images and tables have alt text or captions
- [`split_markdown()`](https://wyuill.github.io/knittogether/reference/split_markdown.md)
  : Split a long Markdown file into one file per section
